status: pre-registration for Q2 and Q3, committed before q2_q3.py is run on the study data
disclosure: Some contrasts were already seen in the audit tool during exploration on 2026-10-13 (the klein distillation row of the contrast overview; SDXL -> SDXL-Turbo saturation with opposite per-subject shifts; Qwen-Image framing closer; SDXL painting-like, muted and busy). Q2 and Q3 are therefore confirmatory only in the sense that their rules are fixed before the scripted run; the paper reports them as pre-specified descriptive analyses, not as blind tests. Q1 is the only blind primary analysis.
inherits: frozen_margins.json (definitions of Delta and log IQR ratio, margins 0.5 and log 1.5, equivalence rules), frozen_aspects.json (sat, medium, shot, tone, bg), frozen_scale.json (s_aspect, never recomputed). Main prompts only (24 subjects).
seed_pairing: As in frozen_margins.json: seeds are resampled jointly for A and B only when both are the same checkpoint; otherwise A and B are resampled independently (G07 -> G08 is therefore unpaired, although the two pipelines start from the same noise).

Q3.question: What does a distillation package change? (RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md section 3)
Q3.primary_case: klein 4B package: G07_klein_base4b_cfg1 -> G08_klein4b (checkpoint, steps 50 -> 4; CFG 1 in both)
Q3.tests: median over subjects of Delta and of log IQR ratio, 5 aspects x 2 effects = 10 tests, Holm-corrected within Q3 (separately from Q1)
Q3.bootstrap: 10,000 replicates, seed 20261014, subjects resampled within categories, seeds resampled independently for A and B; 90% percentile intervals; two-sided bootstrap p as in q1_primary.py
Q3.descriptive_packages: G11_klein_base9b -> G12_klein9b (klein 9B package) and G02_sdxl -> G03_sdxl_turbo (SDXL -> Turbo: checkpoint, scheduler, steps 50 -> 1, CFG 5 -> 0, 1024 -> 512 px). Same estimates and 90% intervals, no p values; label 'same place' / 'same spread' if the interval lies within the margin, 'beyond margin' if the whole interval lies beyond it, otherwise 'unresolved'. Never attributed to one setting.
Q3.reversals: for every Q3 contrast and aspect: number of subjects whose own shift is at least 0.5 in the direction opposite to the pooled median shift, with a per-subject 90% seed-bootstrap interval (2,000 replicates) that excludes 0

Q2.question: Where do configurations at their recommended settings settle, how far apart are they, and do the differences persist across subjects? Descriptive; no attribution to family, scale or architecture.
Q2.location: L_gs = (median of configuration g on subject s - centre_s) / s_aspect, where centre_s is the median over the 8 configurations of their medians on subject s. Typical location of g = median over subjects of L_gs; typical spread of g = median over subjects of IQR_gs / s_aspect.
Q2.pairwise: for each of the 28 pairs and each aspect: median over subjects of Delta with a 90% hierarchical bootstrap interval; label as in the descriptive packages ('same place', 'beyond margin', 'unresolved'). Reported: the number of pairs beyond the margin per aspect.
Q2.subject_dependent_default: configuration g has a subject-dependent default on an aspect if at least 3 subjects have L_gs >= +0.5 and at least 3 subjects have L_gs <= -0.5, each with a per-subject 90% seed-bootstrap interval (2,000 replicates; centre held fixed) that excludes 0 on that side
Q2.hidden_opposite_shifts: a pair hides opposite shifts on an aspect if its pooled median Delta is within the margin (|Delta| < 0.5) while at least 3 subjects shift by >= +0.5 and at least 3 by <= -0.5, each with a per-subject 90% seed-bootstrap interval excluding 0. Reported also for the Q3 contrasts. These are the T2 cases (pooled vs per subject).
Q2.bootstrap: 2,000 replicates, seed 20261015, subjects resampled within categories (the same subject draw for all configurations in a replicate), seeds resampled independently per configuration; the centre is recomputed in every replicate
Q2.multiplicity: none: Q2 is descriptive and carries no p values
